questions.question: Does the coarser microstructure observed at interlayer boundaries in PBF-LB/M W20Mo20Ta20Nb20V20 result in a localized reduction in microhardness compared to the bulk, and is this reduction driven by the lower growth rates and temperature gradients at outer contours?
questions.rationale: Confirming the mechanical impact of interlayer boundary coarseness is critical for determining if a post-process heat treatment or modified scan strategy is needed to homogenize the mechanical properties across the build.
questions.decision_use: Decide whether to implement a remelting step or modify scan strategies to mitigate boundary softening.
answer_requirements: Spatially resolved microhardness mapping across the interlayer boundary vs. the bulk
SEM/EBSD analysis to correlate local grain size and morphology with hardness measurements
evidence_spans: According to [ [51] ] temperature gradients in the liquid and growth rates are smaller at the outer contours of the meltpool compared to the inner regions, explaining the coarser structures
The microhardness of the PBF-LB/M A sample with the coarser structure is 561 ± 17 HV0.1 (n = 9)
while the microhardness of the PBF-LB/M B sample is 614 ± 21 HV0.1 (n = 9).
